items.work: Serenade for Tenor, Horn and Strings, Op. 31
items.performers: Peter Pears, tenor; Barry Tuckwell, horn; London Symphony Orchestra; Benjamin Britten, conductor
items.label: Decca
items.note: A solo horn frames settings of English poetry about night, sleep and dreams. Pears sings the part Britten wrote for him, with the composer conducting the London Symphony strings; his handling of the poems is the main reason to choose this recording first. Barry Tuckwell is an equal partner in the horn’s exposed calls, around Blake’s rose and in the last offstage echo.

items.performers: Peter Pears, Claire Watson, James Pease, Jean Watson, Raymond Nilsson, Owen Brannigan, Lauris Elms, Geraint Evans, John Lanigan, David Kelly, Marion Studholme and Iris Kells; Orchestra and Chorus of the Royal Opera House, Covent Garden; Benjamin Britten, conductor
items.label: Decca
items.note: A Suffolk fishing village turns against a fisherman after the deaths of his apprentices. Britten conducts Peter Pears, the tenor who created Grimes, with Claire Watson as Ellen Orford; it is the first choice for the words. Pears makes Grimes’s speech as troubling as his singing, and Britten keeps the Borough scenes at a brisk pace around him.

items.performers: Galina Vishnevskaya, soprano; Peter Pears, tenor; Dietrich Fischer-Dieskau, baritone; Simon Preston, organ; The Bach Choir and London Symphony Chorus, chorus master David Willcocks; Highgate School Choir, director Edward Chapman; Melos Ensemble; London Symphony Orchestra; Benjamin Britten, conductor
items.label: Decca
items.note: Britten interrupts the Latin Mass with Wilfred Owen’s poems, which Pears and Fischer-Dieskau sing with a chamber ensemble; Vishnevskaya is heard in contrast. His recording finally brought together the three soloists he had wanted for Coventry.
